neighbours.label: ' know' in the idiom 'you never know' (also 'one never knows'); 'know' without 'never' and 'never' with other verbs stay quiet.
fire: Keep the receipt, because you never know.
Buy a lottery ticket now and then; you never know.
Bring a spare tyre on long trips, you never know when you'll need it.
Talk to the stranger at the bus stop, you never know who they are.
Save some money each month, since you never know what will happen.
Send in the application anyway, you never know.
Keep the old cables in a drawer, you never know.
Ask the shop if they have it in the back, you never know.
quiet: Keep the receipt, because I know you might return it.
Buy a lottery ticket now and then; it's only a dollar.
Bring a spare tyre on long trips, you never see a garage out there.
Talk to the stranger at the bus stop, they might know the way.
Save some money each month, since prices keep rising.
Send in the application anyway, you never lose anything by trying.
Keep the old cables in a drawer, you might need them.
Ask the shop if they have it in the back, they usually know.

notes: Card: ' know' x20, ' knows' x12; deterministic pair cover held (AUROC 1.00, covers 50%) for ' never| know'. Exploratory probe: 'you never know' 0.82; 'You know what I mean' 0.001; 'You never see' 0.001; 'Nobody knows' 0.000.
